script.text: Alright, we're live. Topic: is laser collimation actually better than a cheshire, or do we all just like gadgets.
Genuinely though — I'm a beginner with a 6-inch dob and I cannot tell if my views are bad because of collimation or because of my sky. How do you separate those?
That's the best question anyone's asked in one of these. Short version: collimation errors are symmetric and always present. Sky problems come and go with conditions.
Star test on a bright star at high magnification. If the diffraction rings are off-center, that's collimation. If they're shimmering but concentric, that's seeing.
Nobody has ever explained it to me that clearly. That's genuinely going to change how I diagnose a bad session.
That's the whole point of doing these in text. That exchange doesn't happen in a 400-person audio room.
Room's open. Thesis: every 'instant finality' claim in this industry is a p50 number wearing a p99 costume.
Counterpoint: for the vast majority of transaction values, p50 is the correct number to design against. Not everything needs settlement-grade guarantees.
isn't the actual problem that nobody publishes p99 at all, so integrators literally cannot make that tradeoff even if they wanted to
